articles.title: Systematic debugging for AI agents: Introducing the AgentRx framework
articles.summary: As AI agents transition from simple chatbots to autonomous systems capable of managing cloud incidents, navigating complex web interfaces, and executing multi-step API workflows, a new challenge has emerged: transparency. When a human makes a mistake, we can usually trace the logic. articles.title: GitHub Releases · Crush: v0.48.0
articles.summary: # Notifications, CLI-based session management, and more :wave: Hello all! This is a fairly beefy release with a some nice features and a slew of bugfixes. ## Notifications Sometimes LLMs take a while to do so things and, naturally, we go and do other things in the meantime. Now, Crush will send a notification when it needs your attention (e.g. permission requests) and when it finishes its work. How thoughtful! If you find this annoying, it's easy to toggle notifs on and off, too: This feature was implemented by star contributor @Amolith, who waited _so_ patiently for us to QA this incredibly tricky feature across the various platforms we support. ## Sessions on the CLI for humans and agents We're big believers in `crush run`, Crush's non-interactive mode, and this release brings a host of session-based features to the CLI for humans and agents alike.
